title: プログラミングⅢ
subtitle: Programming III
educationalGoal: Learn object-oriented concepts, programming, and application development with the Java language. Programming corresponds to the implementation phase of the software development process. This course uses the learning results of 'Programming I' and 'Programming II'. The results obtained from this course can be used in 'Software Engineering I'.
advice: In this course, students will learn about object-oriented development methods such as classes, inheritance, and encapsulation through learning object-oriented programming using Java language. They will also develop applications and understanding of practical Java functions. Specific items are as follows. 1. Understand object-oriented concepts and features 2. Learn object-oriented programming notation using Java 3. Create applications using a package 4. Learn development methods through application development Please note the following: - Bring your own laptop computer. - Try textbook examples and sample programs to see how they work. - If there is a lack of programming or development tool operation skills, ensure enough review time.
books: Textbooks: Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: The prerequisite skills for this course are the basics of the Java language and how to create a program. Review the second half of 'Programming II (Java language basics) as it will be the prerequisite knowledge for this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand object-oriented terms, Java language notation, and API specifications.
Be able to understand and explain object-oriented concepts such as classes, inheritance, and polymorphism.
Be able to write classes, instances, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism in the Java language.
Be able to create applications using packages and explain development methods.

achievementLevels.standard: The following three goals can be achieved: 1) Be able to explain the terms used in object-oriented programming. 2) Be able to perform learned object-oriented programming. 3) Be able to search for information on Java functions and packages required for Java application development.
